summary: Ran all seven executable acceptance tests for M1-S01 and both always-on structural checks. Four declared skill checkers exited 0 with the exact output the plan predicted from its fixture runs; check-outputs confirmed all 12 declared outputs present, non-empty and parseable; the always-on xml check parsed 11 of 11 XML files; the always-on manifest check found package.xml consistent in both directions (10 members to 10 metadata files, no wildcards, no orphans). Two manual tests were deferred to the M1 gate with their Given/When/Then shape verified and their on-disk evidence gathered, including the Case org-wide default. Nothing failed; the step was moved to tested.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 HIGH: every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every verdict came from an exit code this agent observed. No command was refused, no coverage-gap exclusion was applied, and check-outputs reported nothing missing, empty or malformed.

process_observations.observation: Every checker's actual output matched the output the plan's test description predicted from its fixture run, so the plan's testability claims were evidence rather than assertion.

The skills symlink in the build directory made all four declared checker commands resolve verbatim alongside artefacts/M1-S01, so no command needed rewriting and the deny-list's run-or-refuse rule had no third case to handle.

metadata-builder documented the weakest link in its own manifest rather than leaving it to be found downstream, naming the CompactLayout member form as the thinnest grounding and telling the reader to verify it against a retrieve.

artefacts/M1-S01/deploy-order.md is written by metadata-builder on every run but is not declared in the step's outputs[], so check-outputs never confirms it and a run that silently stopped producing it would look identical to one that did.

Two of the four declared checkers exit 0 over an empty directory, which the plan's own test descriptions record as W09; their exit codes carry weight here only because the always-on xml and manifest checks independently prove the files exist.

check_record_type_layouts.py reported 0 layout(s), so at step scope it proved record-type internal consistency but exercised no record-type-to-layout cross-reference; that assertion rests entirely on M1's milestone test at --manifest-dir artefacts.

package.xml qualifies RecordType, BusinessProcess and CustomField members with the object name but lists the compact layout bare as Case_Intake, and no skill in this agent's reading list carries a non-wildcard CompactLayout member example to settle which form is correct.

The businessProcess filenames use underscores (Support_Process) while their fullName elements and manifest members use spaces (Case.Support Process), so the manifest check had to read fullName from inside each file rather than derive the member from the filename stem.

The Wave 10 markdown and JSON pair under docs/reports/step-tester/ was not written because the caller scoped this run to the build directory only; the build-layer envelope pair under envelopes/M1-S01/ was written in full.
M1-S01 is now tested with two manual tests outstanding and its own human gate still to be taken, so the documentation pass is the next stage of the loop.
process_observations.followup_reason: The step is tested, so PLAN.md, the workbook, decisions.md and traceability.md need the M1-S01 rows before the milestone can be verified.

process_observations.observation: Both deferred manual tests and the record-type-to-layout cross-reference are assertions no step-scoped test in this step can carry.
process_observations.followup_reason: It collects the deferred manual lines into the human checklist and runs M1's build-scoped tests that this step's scope could not reach.
